data.q: Which operator is commonly used for primitive type narrowing in TypeScript?
data.e: The `typeof` operator narrows string, number, boolean, symbol, undefined, function, and bigint types.

data.q: What does the `instanceof` type guard narrow?
data.e: `instanceof` checks the prototype chain and narrows to a specific class or constructor function type.

data.q: Which type guard uses the `in` operator?
data.e: The `in` operator narrows types based on whether a property exists on an object.

data.q: A user-defined type guard function returns which type predicate?
data.e: A type predicate `value is Type` tells TypeScript that if the function returns true, the argument is of `Type`.

data.q: What is a discriminated union in TypeScript?
o: A union of types with a common literal property
data.e: Discriminated unions share a common literal property (the discriminant) that TypeScript uses to narrow the union members.

data.q: Which equality check narrows types in TypeScript?
data.e: Strict equality (`===` and `!==`) narrows types; loose equality (`==` and `!=`) does not because of type coercion.

o: Removes null and undefined from a union
data.e: Truthiness narrowing removes all falsy values (false, 0, '', null, undefined, NaN) from a union when used in an `if` condition.

data.q: What is the purpose of the `never` type in exhaustiveness checking?
o: To represent a value that never occurs
To throw an error at runtime
To ensure all union members are handled
data.e: Assigning a narrowed value to `never` in a `default` clause causes a compile error if not all union members are handled.

data.q: In a switch statement on a discriminated union, what happens if a case is missing?
o: TypeScript shows an error if the discriminant is assigned to `never` in default
data.e: With a `default` case assigning the discriminant to `never`, TypeScript will error if any union member is not handled.

data.q: Which of the following is a valid custom type guard for checking if a value is an array of strings?
o: function isStringArray(val: any): val is string[] { return Array.isArray(val) && val.every(v => typeof v === 'string'); }
function isStringArray(val: any): boolean { return Array.isArray(val); }
function isStringArray(val: any): val is string[] { return typeof val === 'object'; }
function isStringArray(val: any): string[] { return val; }
data.e: A proper type guard uses `val is string[]` and performs runtime checks to ensure the value matches the type.
